SARS-CoV-2: The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
Furosemide: Pfizer. Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a loop diuretic medication used to treat edema due to heart failure, liver scarring, or kidney disease.
In which country is Māori language?
Māori language: New Zealand. The southernmost member of the Austronesian language family, it is related to Cook Islands Māori, Tuamotuan, and Tahitian.
Who is credited with discovering Infrared?
Infrared: William Herschel. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Who is credited with discovering Cherenkov radiation?
Cherenkov radiation: Sergey Vavilov. A classic example of Cherenkov radiation is the characteristic blue glow of an underwater nuclear reactor.
Who is credited with discovering Argon?
Argon: William Ramsay. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Made of adenine bonded to a sugar, this RNA building block underlies ATP, the cell's main energy currency, and doubles as an IV treatment for certain cardiac arrhythmias — what is it?
Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
This white crystalline chemical compound is mainly used as a high-nitrogen agricultural fertilizer, but is also a key ingredient in explosive mixtures used for mining and quarrying — what is it?
Ammonium nitrate is a chemical compound with the formula NH4NO3.
The 16th-largest family of flowering plants, this aromatic group includes cumin, fennel, and coriander alongside deadly relatives like water hemlock — which family?
Apiaceae is a family of mostly aromatic flowering plants named after the type genus Apium, and commonly known as the celery, carrot, or parsley family, or simply as umbellifers.
Technically a giant member of the grass family, this plant's tallest species can grow stalks over 150 feet long and weigh up to 450 kilograms — what plant is it?
Bamboo are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.
This brittle, silvery-white post-transition metal can develop a vividly iridescent, rainbow-colored surface from thin-film oxidation when heated. What element is it?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
One of only two elements liquid at room temperature, this reddish-brown, pungent-smelling element takes its name from the Greek word for 'stench.' What element is it (symbol Br)?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Standardized worldwide in 1907 as exactly 200 milligrams, this unit of mass is used to weigh gemstones and pearls, and is divisible into 100 smaller 'points' — what unit is it?
Carat (mass) (ct) is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg (0.00705 oz; 0.00643 ozt), which is used for measuring gemstones and pearls.
Along with the bonobo, which great ape of equatorial Africa's forests and savannas is humans' closest living relative, according to DNA and fossil evidence?
Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.

Making up 25 to 35 percent of protein content in mammals, this triple-helix structural protein is the main component of the extracellular matrix in cartilage, bone, tendons, and skin — name the protein?
Collagen is the main structural protein in the extracellular matrix of the connective tissues of many animals.
This breaded, deep-fried snack binds a thick sauce like béchamel with fillings such as meat, seafood, or cheese, and was originally a way to use up leftovers — what is it?
Croquette is a deep-fried roll originating in French cuisine and most extended in Spanish cuisine consisting of a thick binder combined with a filling, which is then breaded.
Mother of Princess Alia, this royal later remarried a senior PLO official in 1970 after her short-lived marriage to Jordan's king ended — who is she?
Dina bint Abdul-Hamid (15 December 1929 - 21 August 2019) was a Hashemite princess and Queen of Jordan from 1955 until 1957 as the first wife of King Hussein.
Discovered to have two undescribed relatives only in 2019, this Amazonian 'knifefish' is best known for generating powerful electric discharges — which species?
Electrophorus electricus is the best-known species of electric eel. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
Aerobic exercise, laughter, dancing, and romantic love can all induce this intense feeling of well-being — which is also, less happily, a symptom of mania — what state is it?
Euphoria (yoo-) is the experience (or affect) of pleasure or excitement and intense feelings of well-being and happiness.
Madagascar's largest carnivore, this slender, long-tailed mammal evolved cougar-like features independently and climbs trees head-first thanks to flexible ankles — what is it?
Fossa (animal) (Cryptoprocta ferox; FOSS- or) is a slender, long-tailed, cat-like mammal that is endemic to Madagascar.
This flowering plant genus, whose name derives from the Latin word for a small sword, belongs to the iris family and is centered on the Cape Floristic Region of South Africa — which genus?
Gladiolus (from Latin, the diminutive of gladius, a sword) is a genus of perennial cormous flowering plants in the iris family (Iridaceae).
These seed-loving rodents come in 19 species, the golden or Syrian variety being the one most often found in a child's bedroom cage — what are they?
Hamster are rodents (order Rodentia) belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae, which contains 19 species classified in seven genera.

Despite resembling a common shellfish, this ancient arthropod is actually a chelicerate more closely related to spiders and scorpions, and is often called a 'living fossil' for its unchanged ancient body plan — what is it?
Horseshoe crab are arthropods of the family Limulidae and the only surviving xiphosurans.
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length is often understood as roughly the width of a human thumb — name the unit?
Inch (symbol: in or) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.
This self-described 'constitutional law attorney' joined Trump's inner circle in November 2019, though reporters found she'd never argued a federal case — who is she?
Jenna Ellis (born November 1, 1984) is an American conservative suspended lawyer who was a member of Donald Trump's 2020 re-election campaign's legal team.

First described in 1845 by a German physicist, these two fundamental equalities govern how current and voltage behave in an electrical network, building on Georg Ohm's earlier work — what are they called?
Kirchhoff's circuit laws are two equalities that deal with the current and potential difference (commonly known as voltage) in the lumped element model of electrical circuits.
A Ming-dynasty naturalist poured 27 years into a sprawling pharmacology compendium of nearly 1,900 entries, 11,000 prescriptions, and over a thousand herbs — who was this herbalist and physician?
Li Shizhen (July 3, 1518 - 1593), courtesy name Dongbi, was a Chinese acupuncturist, herbalist, naturalist, pharmacologist, physician, and writer of the Ming dynasty.
About 90% of its cases fall into the non-Hodgkin variety, and its tell-tale signs include painless swollen lymph nodes and night sweats — which group of white-blood-cell cancers is this?
Lymphoma is a group of blood and lymph tumors that develop from lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).

Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German theoretical physicist is considered the originator of quantum theory and one of the founders of modern physics — who is he?
Max Planck (23 April 1858 - 4 October 1947) was a German theoretical physicist.
Widowed in 2021, this Israeli-American billionaire physician publishes Israel Hayom and has been among the most prominent financial supporters of a US president since 2016 — who is she?
Miriam Adelson (ne Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.

Native to the Horn of Africa and nicknamed the 'sand puppy,' this burrowing rodent is the only mammal that's a cold-blooded thermoconformer — and lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen. What is it?
Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber), also known as the sand puppy, is a burrowing rodent native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya, notably in Somali regions.
Also called the coypu, this plant-eating rodent digs streamside burrows and now troubles several countries as an invasive species far from its South American home — what is it?
Nutria (Myocastor coypus) is an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent from South America.

Covered in large protective keratin scales, these mammals — sometimes called scaly anteaters — range across Asia and sub-Saharan Africa and are the only mammal order known to have such scales — what are they?
Pangolin are mammals of the order Pholidota. The one extant family, the Manidae, has three genera: Manis, Phataginus, and Smutsia.
A self-described socialist active in Finland's Pirate Party, this entrepreneur co-founded a famous file-sharing search engine and later started the privacy service Njalla — who is he?
Peter Sunde (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.
Emerging roughly 203 million years ago and wiped out alongside the dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this order of long-necked marine reptiles ruled Jurassic seas — what were they?
Plesiosaur are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
This rose-family genus of roughly 340 species includes almonds, apricots, and cherries, whose pit encloses a kernel that's edible in some species and poisonous in others — which genus?

Prunus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs from the family Rosaceae, with about 340 accepted species (as of March 2024) that include peaches and nectarines, apricots, plums, cherries and almonds.
The only member of the genus Rangifer, this circumpolar deer of the Arctic tundra goes by another name entirely in North America — what is it?
Reindeer (Rangifer tarandus) is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America.
A botanist active in Japan's Meiji era, this scholar died in 1899 after decades of scientific work — who was he?
Ryōkichi Yatabe (October 13, 1851 - August 8, 1899) was a Japanese botanist during the Meiji era.
Applied practically by Archimedes for the quadrature of a parabola, what do we call the addition of infinitely many terms, one after another, central to calculus?
Series (mathematics) is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Known in Hispanic America as guanábana and easily killed by a touch of frost, which Annona fruit blends flavors of strawberry, apple, and sour citrus?
Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanbana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
The only surviving tiger population in the Sunda Islands, found on the Indonesian island of Sumatra after its Bali and Javan cousins went extinct in the 20th century — what is it?
Sumatran tiger is a population of Panthera tigris sondaica on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.

Governed by four fundamental laws relating heat, work and temperature to energy and entropy, this branch of physics underpins chemical, mechanical and biochemical engineering alike — which field of physics?
Thermodynamics is a branch of physics that deals with heat, work, and temperature, and their relation to energy, entropy, and the physical properties of matter and radiation.
Several highly prized truffle species belong to this fungal genus, whose lineage is estimated to date to the close of the Jurassic period — which genus?
Tuber (fungus) is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

Commanding the first spaceflight to carry multiple crew members in 1964, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first human to die during a space mission when his capsule's parachute failed on reentry in 1967 — who was he?
Vladimir Komarov (16 March 1927 - 24 April 1967) was a Soviet test pilot, aerospace engineer, and cosmonaut.

This Polish-American scholar served as Jimmy Carter's national security advisor from 1977 to 1981 and helped organize an influential international policy group known as the Trilateral Commission — who is he?
Zbigniew Brzezinski (March 28, 1928 - May 26, 2017) was a Polish-American diplomat and political scientist.
This term for cancer that begins in gland cells applies to the most common form of breast cancer and one of the two major types of esophageal cancer — which term?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma: Cancer of epithelial cells with glandular origin or characteristics.

Often called the greatest mathematician of the twentieth century, this German-born Frenchman revolutionized algebraic geometry before abruptly leaving his post at a Paris research institute in 1970 — who is he?
This memory disorder comes in two main forms — one blocking recall of events before a specific date, the other preventing new experiences from becoming lasting memories — what is it?
Amnesia: Cognitive disorder where memory is disturbed or lost.
Central to the 18th-century chemical revolution, this French nobleman named oxygen in 1778 and overturned the phlogiston theory of combustion — who is he?
Antoine Lavoisier: French nobleman and chemist (1743–1794)
This order of even-toed hoofed mammals turns out to include whales and dolphins, molecular biology having revealed their close kinship to hippos — what order is it?
Artiodactyla: Order of mammals. Artiodactyla ( AR-tee-oh-DAK-tih-lə; from Ancient Greek ἄρτιος ártios 'even' and δάκτυλος dáktylos 'finger, toe') is an order of placental mammals.
Native to the steppes of Central Asia, this two-humped pack animal's cold and drought tolerance made it indispensable to Silk Road caravans — what is it?
Bactrian camel: Species of mammal of Asia.
Known as silver birch for its peeling white bark, this deciduous tree native to Europe and Asia has become invasive in parts of North America — which species?
Betula pendula: Species of birch. Its range extends into Siberia, China, and southwest Asia in the mountains of northern Turkey, the Caucasus, and northern Iran.

A four-engined American heavy bomber from the 1930s, it dropped more tonnage than any other aircraft in World War II and ranks as the third-most produced bomber in history, after the B-24 and German Ju 88—what is this legendary aircraft?

Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress: American heavy bomber aircraft. The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
Also known as undulant fever or Malta fever, this disease is usually caught by drinking unpasteurized milk from infected animals and tends to persist for life — what is it?
Present in the gut or mouth of up to 60 percent of healthy adults, this opportunistic yeast turns dangerous in immunocompromised patients, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans: Species of fungus. Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
Named after a Louisiana parish and named the state's official canine in 1979, this herding breed was traditionally used to hunt feral boars — what breed is it?
Catahoula Leopard Dog: American breed of dog.
Nicknamed 'Vigorous Dragon' and known to NATO as the Firebird, this Chinese delta-wing, canard-design fighter jet has been exported to Pakistan's air force — which aircraft, capable of Mach 1.8?
Chengdu J-10: Chinese multi-role fighter aircraft family.
Patented in 1967, this sympathomimetic drug helps people with asthma and other breathing disorders by acting as a bronchodilator — which substance?
Clenbuterol: Chemical compound which aids breathing.
The largest living bird species, this flightless native of Africa is one of just two living species in its genus — which bird?
Common ostrich: Species of flightless bird. The common ostrich is one of two extant species of ostriches, the only living members of the genus Struthio in the ratite group of birds.

An incurable, always fatal neurodegenerative disease belonging to the transmissible spongiform encephalopathy group, it causes early symptoms like memory problems, behavioral changes, and poor coordination, with about 70% of sufferers dying within a year. What disease is it?

This English broadcaster is the only person to have won BAFTA Awards in black-and-white, colour, high-definition, 3D, and 4K — a span made possible by a presenting career that began with Zoo Quest in 1954. Who is this natural historian?
David Attenborough: English broadcaster and natural historian (born 1926)

A lean, wedge-skulled medium canine found in Australia and split off from the New Guinea singing dog, this animal's very classification — dog, wolf, or its own species — is still hotly debated — what is it?
Dingo: Canid species native to Australia.
Belonging to the phylum Annelida and often called a 'nightcrawler' by anglers, this segmented soil-dweller is the classic bait fished from underground burrows — which invertebrate?

This discipline systematically applies science and math to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft, with traditional branches in civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical work — which field?
This small finch native to Europe and Asia is the original species to bear its common English name, and goes by 'plum bird' in Shropshire — what is it?
Eurasian bullfinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
Native to North African deserts from Western Sahara to the Sinai, this diminutive canid uses its oversized ears to shed heat and detect prey burrowing underground — which species is it?
Fennec fox: Species of fox. The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) is a small fox native to the deserts of North Africa, ranging from Western Sahara and Mauritania to the Sinai Peninsula.

Madagascar's largest carnivore is a slender, long-tailed mammal that climbs down trees head-first and has convergently evolved so many cat-like features it's been likened to a small cougar — yet it's no cat. What is it?
Fossa (animal): Cat-like, carnivorous mammal endemic to Madagascar.

This digestive disorder involves weak stomach muscle contractions that delay how quickly food empties into the intestine, often linked to nerve damage from uncontrolled diabetes — what's the condition called?
Gastroparesis: Medical condition. The opposite of this, where stomach contents exit quickly into the duodenum, is called dumping syndrome.
The simplest and only non-chiral of the 20 proteinogenic amino acids, this compound makes up about 35% of collagen's amino acid content — what is it?
Glycine: Amino acid. In the body, glycine plays several crucial roles.
Breeders prefer to call it a 'cavy,' and despite its name it hails from the Andes rather than West Africa and isn't related to swine at all — which Andean rodent is it?
Guinea pig: Domesticated rodent from South America.
Comprising cicadas, aphids, bed bugs, and more than 80,000 other species with piercing-sucking mouthparts, which insect order is nicknamed the 'true bugs'?
Hemiptera: Order of insects often called true bugs.
Often called the founder of alpinism and modern meteorology, this Genevan scientist is also credited with building the first successful solar oven — who was he?
Horace Bénédict de Saussure: Genevan scientist and mountaineer (1740–1799)
Marked in its severe stage by hallucinations and paradoxical undressing, which condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35 degrees Celsius?
Hypothermia: Human body core temperature below 35 °C (95 °F)
Known historically as green vitriol or copperas, this blue-green heptahydrate salt is used to treat anemia and forms a paramagnetic octahedral complex in water — which compound?
Iron(II) sulfate: Chemical compound. Iron(II) sulfate or ferrous sulfate (British English: sulphate instead of sulfate) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4·xH2O.

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.

Known to NATO by the reporting name Hokum A and nicknamed 'Black Shark' for its distinctive coaxial rotors, this Russian single-seat attack helicopter has a rare rescue ejection system — which aircraft?
Kamov Ka-50: Attack helicopter. It was designed in the 1980s and adopted for service in the Russian army in 1995.
This broadly distributed genus of spiders is informally known as the widow spiders, including the black widow and brown widow — what is it called?
Latrodectus: Genus of spiders. Latrodectus is a broadly distributed genus of spiders informally called the widow spiders, with several species that are commonly known as the true widows.
This big cat of the genus Panthera now ranges only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India, and is unusual among wild cats for living in social groups — what is it?
Lion: Large cat native to Africa and India.
Able to breathe air thanks to lobed fins and a well-developed internal skeleton, these freshwater vertebrates are considered the closest living relatives of land animals — what are they?
With horn-shaped fins on its head and one of the highest brain-to-body ratios of any fish, this filter-feeding giant may even recognize itself in a mirror — which creature?
Made up of the dura, arachnoid, and pia mater, these three protective membranes shield the brain and spinal cord while containing cerebrospinal fluid — what are they called?
Meninges: Three membranes protecting the brain. In anatomy, the meninges (sing. meninx; from Ancient Greek μῆνινξ (mêninx) 'membrane') are protective membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord.

Soviet pilots called it the "Balalaika" because its planform looked like the stringed instrument, while Poles dubbed it "Ołówek" — the pencil — for its slender fuselage; which most-produced supersonic jet in history earned all those nicknames?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: 1956 Soviet fighter aircraft family.
Drawn from the latex of opium poppies, this naturally occurring opiate acts straight on the central nervous system to dull pain — but risks dependence and tolerance. What is it?
Morphine: Pain medication of the opiate family.
This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, bringing on excessive daytime sleepiness, sleep paralysis, and sudden episodes of muscle collapse called cataplexy — what is it?
Narcolepsy: Human sleep disorder. Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep–wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.
A catecholamine whose very name nods to the kidney, it acts as both a hormone and neurotransmitter and is called "noradrenaline" outside the US — what is it?
Norepinephrine: Catecholamine hormone and neurotransmitter. The general function of norepinephrine is to mobilize the brain and body for action.
Its Greek name means 'serpent-bearer,' and it's depicted as a man grasping a snake represented by a neighboring constellation — which constellation straddles the celestial equator?
Ophiuchus: Constellation straddling the celestial equator. Ophiuchus ( o-fee-YOO-kəs) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
This butterfly was the first species to be given the common name now applied to its entire family, and is widespread across the Palearctic and North America — which species?
Papilio machaon: Species of insect. Papilio machaon, the Old World swallowtail, is a butterfly of the family Papilionidae.
In placental mammals, this is the region of the body between the anus and the genitals, running from the pubic bone to the tailbone, and is often considered an erogenous zone — what is it called?
Perineum: Region of the body between the genitals and anus. The perineum (pl.: perineums or perinea) in placental mammals is the space between the anus and the genitals.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie: French physicist and chemist (1859–1906)
Also called quaking aspen for the way its leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, which poplar species is native to the Old World's cool temperate regions?
Nicknamed 'gold cap' and 'golden halo,' this is the world's best-known psilocybin-containing mushroom thanks to its wide distribution and how easily it's cultivated — which species?
Psilocybe cubensis: Species of fungus. It belongs to the fungus family Hymenogastraceae and was previously known as Stropharia cubensis.
Also known as steelhead in its sea-run form, this North American Pacific species shows off a vivid reddish stripe along its flank in breeding males — which fish?
Rainbow trout: Fresh-water species of fish.
His 'Essai Sur La Nature Du Commerce' was called the 'cradle of political economy'; this Irish-French banker made a fortune speculating in John Law's Mississippi Company — who is it?
Richard Cantillon: Irish-French economist and banker (c. 1680 – 1734)
This extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period had closely-spaced eyes at the front of its head, 'like car headlamps,' and is best known from fossils found in Bolivia — what is it?
Sacabambaspis: Extinct genus of jawless fishes.
Comprising seven species from the flatback to the leatherback, five of these ocean-dwelling reptiles are threatened with extinction — what are they?
Sea turtle: Reptiles of the superfamily Chelonioidea.
This small, wingless, primitive insect gets its common name from its grey sheen and darting, fish-like movements — and its scientific name hints at a diet of sugars and starches. What is it?
Silverfish: Small land insect in the order Zygentoma.
This healthcare discipline treats disorders of voice, fluency, and swallowing, practiced by clinicians licensed under boards overseen by groups like ASHA — which field of study?
Belonging to a fish family whose fossils date back to the Late Cretaceous, these long-lived, late-maturing fish share their order with paddlefish and once swam as far as North Africa — what are they?
Pig-shaped with a short, flexible snout, this odd-toed ungulate mammal lives in the jungles of South and Central America and Southeast Asia, alongside equine and rhino relatives — which animal?
Covered in sharp spikes along its leaf margins to ward off herbivores, this prickly flowering plant's fluffy seed head is known as 'down.' What is it?
Thistle: Common name of a group of flowering plants.
Sold as Tramal, this opioid painkiller doubles as an SNRI — which means it carries a rare risk of serotonin syndrome. What is it?
This hypothetical element 126, nicknamed eka-plutonium, intrigues physicists because 126 may be a 'magic number' of protons sitting near the center of a predicted island of stability — what is it?
Unbihexium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 126 (Ubh)
Native from Morocco and Portugal east to Iran, this flowering plant species includes thousands of varieties whose fruit is eaten fresh or dried into raisins and currants — what species is it?
Vitis vinifera: Species of flowering plant in the grape vine family.
The largest wild member of the dog family, it can still breed fertile hybrids with coyotes and jackals, and counts the domestic dog and dingo among its many subspecies — what animal is it?
The symbol for roentgenium is Rg. Roentgenium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
The symbol for gold is Au. Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au and atomic number 79.
